assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and the subsequent Sr/Yb demonstrations, turned the narrow optical transition into a clock whose fractional uncertainty is at the 10^-18 level. This is a clear, original and lasting advance in measurement: it redefines what can be measured and how accurately, and it underpins tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and the planned redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and first realised the magic-wavelength lattice concept; Ye's group (JILA) drove the systematic uncertainty and stability down to the 10^-18 regime and the dense-ensemble clocks. A two-person prize is clean and well matched to the credited names. Other contributors (for example Lemonde, Hollberg, Hall's comb work already recognised in 2005) could be argued but are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation across several laboratories, species and national metrology institutes; the interpretation is stable and the technology is already deployed. Recognition is timely: the field is mature but still advancing.
uncertainties: I have a documented professional connection to the Hall laboratory milieu (a research stay in John Hall's laboratory) from which Ye emerged; this should be declared but does not change the technical assessment.
Whether credit should also reach the ion-clock or earlier optical-frequency-comb work is a matter of overlap with prior prizes and is not resolved by the supplied names.
My recollection of the precise first-demonstration dates and uncertainty figures is from memory, not independently verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The titanium-sapphire gain medium and the passive mode-locking schemes (Kerr-lens and SESAM) created the compact, robust femtosecond solid-state laser. It is an enabling invention for almost all later ultrafast science, including frequency combs, multiphoton microscopy and attosecond physics, and its originality and breadth of impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Moulton introduced Ti:sapphire as a broadly tunable laser medium; Sibbett's group demonstrated self-mode-locking (Kerr-lens) in Ti:sapphire; Keller invented and developed semiconductor saturable-absorber mode-locking. The three credited names map onto three separable, decisive contributions and fit a three-person prize. Credit around the discovery of Kerr-lens mode-locking (Spence, Kean, Sibbett) and the role of Kerr-lens theory by others is a recognised wrinkle.
assessment.maturity: Thirty to forty years of use, with commercial dominance and many independent implementations; no interpretive instability. Recognition is arguably overdue relative to the 2018 chirped-pulse amplification prize and the 2023 attosecond prize, which both depend on this technology.
uncertainties: The compound nature (gain medium plus two different mode-locking mechanisms) may make a single coherent citation difficult.
Priority and credit for Kerr-lens mode-locking among the Sibbett group members is only partly captured by the supplied names; my recollection is not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of the Z2 topological insulator and the quantum spin Hall effect, together with the HgTe/CdTe experimental realisation, opened a whole class of topological quantum matter. The idea is conceptually original, the prediction was sharp and quantitatively testable, and it has produced a large, durable research programme.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the Z2 classification and quantum spin Hall proposal; Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe wells (with Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang theory, not in the supplied credit). The three names form a natural theory-plus-experiment prize, though Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and the three-dimensional topological insulator experiments (Hasan, Shen and others) are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by transport and ARPES in multiple materials and laboratories over roughly fifteen years; interpretation is stable. The 2016 prize recognised topological phase transitions, so this is a natural, timely follow-up.
uncertainties: The omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang from the supplied credit leaves an attribution question I cannot resolve from the longlist.
Practical impact in devices is still limited; the case rests mainly on conceptual importance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution turned a foundational property of quantum mechanics into a concrete cryptographic protocol (BB84, plus the entanglement-based E91 protocol). The idea is original and has led to commercial systems and satellite links, with clear lasting impact in quantum information science.
assessment.attribution: BB84 is the joint work of Bennett and Brassard; Ekert's 1991 entanglement-based protocol is a distinct, decisive contribution connecting QKD to Bell inequalities. The supplied credit lists both 'Artur Ekert' and 'Artur K. Ekert', which I treat as one person and select a single exact string. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is a known credit wrinkle not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Experimental demonstrations are numerous and independent, and the 2022 prize for entangled-photon experiments has already recognised the experimental foundations. Practical security and deployment are still evolving, so recognition may be somewhat early for the application but not for the idea.
uncertainties: The supplied credit contains a duplicated name string for Ekert; I rely on one of them.
Partial overlap with the 2022 prize may weigh against, and the security of real implementations is an open practical matter.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller proposed the trapped-ion quantum gate and the framework for quantum simulation with trapped ions and cold atoms. This is a seminal, original body of theory that guided experiments in two major platforms and gave quantum computation a physical blueprint.
assessment.attribution: The pair are the two clear originators of the ion-trap gate proposal and of the cold-atom simulation proposals; the two-person configuration is clean. The experimental realisation (Wineland, Blatt and others) is partly recognised through the 2012 prize, which reduces the unrecognised remainder.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed over decades by many groups; interpretation is stable. Recognition is mature, and the field is now moving into commercial devices, so timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 Nobel prize for single-quantum-system control and with the cold-atom simulation candidate may complicate the citation.
I treat the details of who first proposed which scheme as recalled knowledge, not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson at the LHC confirmed the last missing particle of the Standard Model and is plainly among the major experimental achievements of the era. Importance, clarity and permanence are all very high.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize recognised the theory; the experimental credit is spread over two collaborations of thousands, and the prize rules limit it to three people. Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee are founding architects of ATLAS and CMS, whereas Gianotti was ATLAS spokesperson at the time of announcement. Any choice is a judgement about leadership versus decisive technical contribution and I cannot settle it from the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: The discovery is firmly confirmed, with properties measured by both experiments and combined; recognition is timely. The constraint is the allocation, not the physics.
uncertainties: The collaboration-scale attribution problem is unresolved; the rules cap laureates at three and any selection is contestable.
The overlapping candidate that stresses the accelerator and detector construction may need to be treated as a compound discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene and moiré flat bands introduced a tunable platform for correlated insulators and superconductivity in a clean two-dimensional system. It is original, conceptually clear and has spawned a large new field.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat band at the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group observed correlated insulating and superconducting states experimentally, with Cao and collaborators as primary authors and with parallel work elsewhere. Theory plus experiment fits a three-person prize, but the contribution of the junior authors and other groups is a recognised sensitivity.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by multiple groups, but the field is young: the origin of the superconductivity and the nature of the correlated states are still debated. I regard recognition as plausible but somewhat early.
uncertainties: The interpretation of the superconducting mechanism is unsettled.
Credit among theory, experiment and the earlier twisted-graphene theory is only partly captured by the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The recollision model explains high-harmonic generation as ionisation, acceleration and return of the electron, and is the conceptual foundation of strong-field and attosecond physics. It is original, simple, quantitatively predictive and has had lasting impact in my own broader field of laser-matter interaction.
assessment.attribution: Corkum's three-step model, Schafer and co-workers' related semiclassical analysis and Lewenstein's quantum strong-field approximation are three separable contributions; the credited trio fits a prize. Credit overlaps with the 2023 attosecond prize, which went to Agostini, Krausz and L'Huillier, and with Kulander's related work, not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed experimentally and widely used. Because the 2023 prize already recognised the experimental attosecond consequences, further recognition of the theory may be seen as partly redundant.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 prize reduces the marginal case.
Whether the three credited names give the right split for the model versus the quantum theory is unresolved.
